Debut collection of creative director Dario Vitale; a passing mention in Wallpaper's 28 Sep 2026 Milan round-up treats Versace as Pieter Mulier's future house, so Vitale has since left (exit not checked here). versace.com not fetched.

Klausner's second womenswear collection for the house. Date consistent with NowFashion (30 Sep 2025, 15:00). No dedicated SS26 show page was found on driesvannoten.com.

notes: Unsigned house text on Lanvin's 'LANVIN SUMMER 2026 SHOW: VERS LE MONDE' page, naming artistic director Peter Copping; his second runway collection for the house after his January 2025 debut. On the first fetch the URL redirected to the lanvin.com homepage; later fetches served the page. No date on the page; Numéro gives the show as 30 September 2025.

excerpt: The Summer 2026 Stella woman is a force of dichotomies; masculine and feminine, grounded yet ethereal. Her wardrobe is one of architectural contrasts and coexistence with nature – crafted with 98% conscious, 100% cruelty-free materials.
themes: coming together for humanity, animals and Mother Earth; masculine and feminine; grounded yet ethereal; architectural contrasts; coexistence with nature; cruelty-free materials
notes: Third-person house text on the 'Come Together: The Summer 2026 Runway Show' page (search listings title it 'Test Trunk'). The page opens: 'Come Together for humanity, animals and Mother Earth – a message from Stella’s heritage in music and activism.' It also names two material launches, FEVVERS and PURE.TECH. No date on the page.

excerpt: To me, this collection is more than just a carefully curated line of clothing and accessories. It is an assemblage of reflections and emotions that embody my own personal growth throughout all these years at Balmain
themes: reflections and emotions; personal growth; years at Balmain; continuity ('Continuum'); return to the venue of his first show
notes: Olivier Rousteing's statement quoted in Numéro (Nathan Merchadier, article titled 'Bohemian style at the Balmain show'), introduced 'Olivier Rousteing explained in a statement'; the quote ends without a full stop in the source. V Magazine gives the title 'Continuum' and says it was the venue of his first Balmain show, the source of the last two themes. This was Rousteing's last Balmain collection: FashionNetwork reported Antonin Tron's appointment on 12 November 2025 'following Olivier Rousteing's departure'. No balmain.com page was reached.

notes: Opening line of the house press release as quoted by The Industry (Tom Bottomley). AnOther (3 Oct 2025) quotes 'Seduction is a dialogue' as his written statement; Numero's English page gives a different rendering ('triggered by a glance'). Show on Wednesday 1 Oct 2025 at Place Vendôme (Numero). Ackermann's second Tom Ford collection (his debut was AW25).

excerpt: I was actually looking at female power. And how often you go to the masculine to empower women.

notes: Sarah Burton (creative director) speaking, block-quoted in The Impression (Kenneth Richard) after a line saying she 'spoke of the collection'; it continues 'When actually, I wanted to go to the female to empower women.' No givenchy.com page found. Burton's second Givenchy collection (her debut was AW25).

The gallery page itself shows no date; 2025-10-06 is the date Dazed's Rei Kawakubo listing page gives it. No byline. Show date not restated.

excerpt: At a time when dialogue is fading, style becomes a form of discourse -- not one that imposes but one that connects and adds nuance
themes: style as a form of discourse; connecting rather than imposing; adding nuance; a time when dialogue is fading
notes: Anthony Vaccarello (creative director), words he wrote in his show notes, quoted in an AFP report carried by FashionNetwork UK (the double hyphen is the source's). The only house statement found; it frames the collection rather than describing the clothes. AnOther (Alexander Fury, 1 Oct 2025) and Numéro (Léa Zetlaoui, 30 Sep 2025) quote no designer words. Shown on the Place du Trocadéro facing the Eiffel Tower on Monday 29 September 2025, between beds of white hydrangeas laid out as the house logo (AFP).

excerpt: This is why I chose Sam’s work on Euphoria to be part of the ClairObscur collection narrative. For its ability to convey a sense of our realities, through a prismatic representation of human fragilities and strengths
themes: ClairObscur; Sam Levinson's Euphoria woven into the collection narrative; human fragilities and strengths; people and the narratives they carry; fragility and imperfection as authenticity; truth, compassion, affinity and humanity
notes: Pierpaolo Piccioli (creative director), quoted in Numéro (Léa Zetlaoui) and followed by 'Pierpaolo Piccioli explained'; the passage before it ('I am deeply interested in people, in the narratives they carry...') is introduced with 'he stated in his show notes', so both probably come from the notes. Wallpaper's live page quotes a Balenciaga statement that the installation and experiential space reflect principles 'central to Levinson and Piccioli – of truth, compassion, affinity and above all humanity'; AnOther (Alexander Fury) quotes 'A fresco of humanity.' Numéro's English page has a French edition, so the English may be a translation. FashionNetwork (Godfrey Deeny, 8 Mar 2026) says Saturday, in a space on the Champs-Élysées; Wallpaper's entry stamped 8 March says 'last night', matching 7 March 2026.

excerpt: No one shines alone. Just like corals, we – and the ideas we champion – need two fundamental elements to flourish: protection and mutual exchange.
themes: no one shines alone; corals; protection and mutual exchange; a safe space where everyone can be heard; turning the fragile into the resilient; joy and light as shared achievements
notes: Pierpaolo Piccioli (creative director), from what FashionNetwork (Olivier Guyot) calls his letter of intent; Wallpaper (7 Oct 2026) calls it a letter to guests and quotes 'No one shines alone' and 'Joy and light are never solitary achievements' in the same words. The letter goes on: 'Providing a safe space means allowing everyone to express themselves and be heard.' FashionNetwork's UK article says it is a translation of a French original, so its English may differ from the letter's own where Wallpaper does not confirm it. Coral pieces in cream, orange, white and pink per the writer. Shown at the Tennis Club de Paris on Thursday afternoon; an earlier FashionNetwork schedule story gave Thursday 1 October at 2pm, matching the date on file.

excerpt: For us, the act of making is, at its core, an expression of joy – an intellectual, process-driven pursuit charged with playfulness
themes: making as an expression of joy; an intellectual, process-driven pursuit; playfulness; play as rigorous experimentation and problem-solving; moving between instinct and experience; craft and innovation driven by curiosity
notes: Jack McCollough and Lazaro Hernandez (creative directors), as quoted on Wallpaper's Paris A/W 2026 live page ('they said'; entry stamped 6 March 2026). AnOther (Alexander Fury, 7 Mar 2026) says the second half 'was actually what the duo wrote', and Wallpaper's 11 March round-up calls the first half part of their statement, hence show notes. The same entry quotes 'It is the idea of play as rigorous experimentation and problem-solving, moving between instinct and experience'. FashionNetwork (Godfrey Deeny, 6 Mar 2026) places the show at the Château de Vincennes on Friday 6 March 2026; AnOther describes a Lurpak-yellow catwalk.

excerpt: We’re taking the vision, the craft, and injecting a reality and character. There’s proximity to the clothes, proximity to living, and proximity to our own sensibility.
themes: vision and craft given reality and character; proximity to the clothes, to living and to their own sensibility; a proposition for dressing; the new Loewe language as a wardrobe; an old-world and new-world conversation
notes: Jack McCollough and Lazaro Hernandez (creative directors), quoted in Wallpaper's round-up of the best Paris S/S 2027 shows (Jack Moss); the passage comes straight after their 'What we’re putting forward here is a proposition for dressing. How does this new Loewe language become a wardrobe?' and the words 'they said'. Wallpaper also gives their phrase 'old-world – new-world conversation'; AnOther (Alexander Fury, 4 Oct 2026) quotes 'New world, old world.' Shown in an in-the-round arena built by Casper Mueller Kneer in the grounds of the Château de Vincennes. No source read states the date; The Impression's show calendar lists Loewe on 2 October, matching the date on file.

excerpt: I love when messy, complex, layered inner lives come through underneath great clothes
themes: messy, layered inner lives under great clothes; people with style who wear beautiful clothes in a personal way; intuition over strategy; rejecting the idea of a concept; style without irony
notes: Michael Rider (creative director): 'wrote Rider in the show notes', as quoted by Alexander Fury in AnOther. The same notes speak of 'thinking about people with style who wear beautiful clothes in a personal way' and 'Intuition over strategy. Feeling it rather than planning it.'; Dazed (11 Mar 2026) quotes the notes' 'style without irony'. Shown in a white box behind the Institut de France (AnOther); FashionNetwork (Godfrey Deeny, 8 Mar 2026) says Saturday and Wallpaper gives 7 March, matching the date on file.

excerpt: So even with the really beautiful gowns, I want them to feel a bit off. It's about reality.
themes: beautiful gowns that feel a bit off; reality; clothes made to be worn on the street; something democratic; never precious; concepts and proposals for real life
notes: Glenn Martens (creative director) in an interview with Wallpaper (Jack Moss) published four months after the show; the sentence before it says the S/S 2026 collection was described as 'a series of concepts and proposals for real life' in the press notes. He also says 'I wanted to do something democratic' and wants the clothes 'never precious'. His first ready-to-wear collection for the house, shown at Le Centquatre (a former funeral parlour in the 19th arrondissement) with a children's orchestra. Dazed (4 Oct 2025) says the show fell on a Saturday and FashionNetwork includes it in its Saturday report, matching 4 October 2025; Numéro calls it day five of fashion week. No words of Martens were found in coverage from the week of the show (Dazed, FashionNetwork, Numéro).

excerpt: Every embroidery, knitted thread, printed motif reveals both the maker's hand and their devotion
themes: Devotion (collection title); embroidery, knitted thread and printed motif; the maker's hand; craft as devotion; clothing that holds emotion and carries memory
notes: Chemena Kamali (creative director): 'she explains in her show notes', quoted in Numéro (Camille Bois-Martin), which gives the collection's title as Devotion. AnOther (Alexander Fury, 11 Mar 2026) quotes her on 'how clothing can both hold emotion, and carry memory'; FashionNetwork paraphrases her inspiration as traditional costume and folkloric craft. Numéro's English page has a French edition and no translation note. FashionNetwork (Godfrey Deeny, 5 Mar 2026) puts the show at UNESCO on Thursday morning, matching the date on file.

excerpt: Movement seems to fracture pieces – choreographies of fringe create silhouettes that shatter and regroup
themes: movement fracturing pieces; choreographies of fringe; silhouettes that shatter and regroup; the woman's body within, moving and alive; clothes that cry; a cocoon of imagery
notes: Pieter Mulier (creative director), 'wrote Mulier' in his SS26 show notes, as quoted in Dazed's Paris SS26 round-up (Hannah Bertolino and Elliot Hoste; Dazed spells him Peter), which adds that he described the offering as 'clothes that cry'. Wallpaper quotes the notes: 'there is a sense, always, of the woman's body within – moving, alive'; FashionNetwork quotes him: 'I wanted to create a cocoon of imagery' and 'Sexy, but always very simple and precise'. Shown at the former Fondation Cartier; FashionNetwork's Saturday report (Godfrey Deeny, 5 Oct 2025) matches 4 October 2025. Mulier showed one more Alaïa collection (AW26) before leaving for Versace.

excerpt: identifies with a house that, according to him, has since its beginnings exalted an architectural and sublime vision of the female body, reflecting a new world for women, centred on dynamism, sensuality and an opulence that is resolutely modern in its minimalism
themes: an architectural and sublime vision of the female body; a new world for women; dynamism; sensuality; an opulence that is modern in its minimalism
notes: House text about creative director Antonin Tron, introduced in Numéro (Léa Zetlaoui) with 'As the show notes explain, Antonin Tron'; the notes speak of him in the third person. Numéro adds that Tron told Vogue his approach was 'minimal opulence'. Numéro's English page has a French edition, so the wording may be a translation. Tron's debut for the house; Numéro: 'On March 4th, 2026, Antonin Tron unveiled his first runway show for Balmain', matching the date on file; no venue given. AnOther's review (Alexander Fury, 5 Mar 2026) carries no direct quotes from him.

excerpt: That's why I leapt at the opportunity to show at Centre Pompidou. Not because I wanted this collection to explicitly centre on the relationship between fashion and art, but because I felt, and feel, that going to a Schiaparelli show should feel like going to a museum: an experience equally inspirational, aspirational, and reassuring
themes: showing at the Centre Pompidou; a show that feels like a museum visit; inspirational, aspirational and reassuring; ready-to-wear mistaken for couture; everyday fashion as art; an antidote to the cheap thrills on our phones
notes: Daniel Roseberry (creative director), from a quotation attributed with 'he said' on Wallpaper's Paris S/S 2026 live page (Jack Moss); the entry says his S/S 2026 show notes recalled people asking 'This is ready-to-wear? I thought I was looking at couture.' and quotes him: 'What felt like a liability now feels like a strength. Why can't fashion – even everyday fashion – be art?' and 'Our phones are a slophouse of cheap thrills, with lifespans no longer than a few hours.' Ready-to-wear show at the Centre Pompidou. Dazed (8 Oct 2025) dates it 'Thursday night (October 2)', matching the date on file, and quotes him: 'Schiaparelli RTW has always existed at the crossroads of commercial potential and creative catharsis'. The live page was first published 1 Oct 2025 and last updated 7 Oct 2025; the entry has no time stamp.

excerpt: Going clear means unsubscribing from the noise, so that what remains is a voice as clear as Barbra Streisand’s on opening night at the Bon Soir in 1962 singing ‘Cry Me a River’
themes: Going Clear (collection title); unsubscribing from the noise; a voice that stays clear; Barbra Streisand singing Cry Me a River at the Bon Soir in 1962; a lesson for any kind of art, including fashion; what Schiaparelli stands for in ready-to-wear
notes: Daniel Roseberry (creative director): 'Roseberry said in a statement on Instagram', as quoted by Dazed (Hannah Bertolino); he adds 'It's a good lesson for any kind of art, including fashion.' Dazed also gives a 'black, bone, and butter' palette and a turn away from the industry's 'promise of status and approval' without saying whose words these are. AFP via FashionNetwork (2 Oct 2026) quotes his introductory note: 'Our couture identity was relatively easy to define' and 'but I admit it was harder to determine who and what Schiaparelli stands for in a highly saturated ready-to-wear market'. Ready-to-wear show at the Louvre (AFP: the Cour Carrée; Dazed: an intimate, cabaret-bar-like space). AFP calls it day four of fashion week; The Impression's calendar lists 1 October, matching the date on file.

excerpt: The silhouettes undulate like waves. The lines overlap and blend together. Figure and background intertwine. A presence that wavers between absence and reality
themes: In Praise of Bamboo Shadows (collection title); silhouettes undulating like waves; overlapping, blending lines; figure and background intertwined; a presence between absence and reality; bamboo
notes: The line is IM MEN (Issey Miyake's men's line), not Homme Plissé. The house's press release as quoted by FashionNetwork (Matthieu Guinebault): the quote is followed by 'stated a press release from the line led by Sen Kawahara, Yuki Itakura, and Nobutaka Kobayashi', three members of the Miyake Design Studio; the release itself was not seen. The UK article says it is a translation, so the English may be FashionNetwork's rendering. Collection titled 'In Praise of Bamboo Shadows'; the writer says bamboo was at the heart of it. Shown inside the Césure cultural space with about forty looks; the article places it on the third day of Paris men's fashion week alongside Givenchy, which it says showed on Thursday, matching 25 June 2026.

excerpt: in a dialogue between music composition and clothes-making, where auditory and visual senses inspire one another to give rise to a more intimate integration of music and clothing.
themes: a dialogue between music composition and clothes-making; auditory and visual senses inspiring one another; an intimate integration of music and clothing; live music at the show; ma, the space between (FashionNetwork's account)
notes: The house's words, introduced 'as the brand explained' in Wallpaper's round-up of the best Paris S/S 2027 shows (Jack Moss, with India Birgitta Jarvis), about a live multi-instrumental piece by a pianist at the show; probably from the show notes, which Wallpaper does not say. Satoshi Kondo is the designer. Shown at the Dojo de Paris (the Institut du Judo, Porte de Châtillon); FashionNetwork (Olivier Guyot, 5 Oct 2026) says Friday, matching 2 October 2026, and frames the collection around ma, but quotes no designer or house words.
